messages.content:
You compare an edited output video against its actual source video, the original user request, and the executed editing instruction. Optional reference assets show the desired editing target.
The historical-source selection in the original user request has already been executed. Evaluate only its editing requirements against the actual videos. Do not treat historical appearance descriptions in that request as observed facts; use the visible source video instead. Compare the original editing requirements with the executed instruction too, so you can identify any omitted or changed constraint introduced when the instruction was normalized.
The output_video_card was produced earlier by independently observing only the output. Treat it as a fixed observation record: do not rewrite it, return a new card, or add intended changes to it. It can be imperfect; inspect the actual videos when comparing.
Call record_edit_result exactly once. Return only its five parameters: requested_change, observed_change, fulfillment, unexpected_changes, uncertain. These describe the source-to-output comparison, not a new video card. Use concise English.
State what was requested and what visibly changed. Use fulfillment=fulfilled, partial, not_fulfilled, or uncertain. Do not infer success from the instruction. Note unintended changes to identity, appearance, action, scene, camera, timing, and image quality when visible. If a reference match or subtle facial change cannot be judged, record the uncertainty rather than assuming success. Do not claim to have inspected missing reference pixels. Do not call an editing tool or regenerate video.
Use one separate XML parameter block for each of the five parameters. The three text parameters contain text. unexpected_changes and uncertain contain JSON arrays of strings, including [] when empty. Do not nest a card or review object inside any parameter.
Structural example only; replace descriptions with your actual comparison:
<tool_call>
<function=record_edit_result>
<parameter=requested_change>Requested edit</parameter>
<parameter=observed_change>Actual visible change</parameter>
<parameter=fulfillment>uncertain</parameter>
<parameter=unexpected_changes>[]</parameter>
<parameter=uncertain>["Any unresolved comparison"]</parameter>
</function>
</tool_call>

Use the provided reference image to determine the viewing direction, subject placement, and framing at the start of the edited video. Follow the camera setup and movement described above, and preserve the timing and progression of the action in the source video. Keep the person's identity, hairstyle, hair color, clothing, expression, action, and scene unchanged. Follow the camera setup and movement described above, and preserve the timing and progression of the action in the source video.","output_video_card":{"observed":{"action":"The character stands in an open paved area, slowly turning her body while raising one or both arms to touch or adjust her hair.","camera":"A medium full-body shot that orbits around the character, keeping her centered while the background shifts.","clothing":"A brown cropped tank top, light beige wide-leg trousers, and dark flat shoes.","hair_color":"Reddish-brown.","hairstyle":"Long, straight hair reaching past the shoulders.","identity":"A slender female 3D character with a slim build and fair skin.","scene":"An outdoor amusement park or fairground with a Ferris wheel, colorful stalls, fences, and trees under bright daylight."},"uncertain":[]}}

arguments.observed_change: The output shows a full-body orbit around the same character, with the background continuously changing from the amusement-park front view through side and rear views and back toward the front. The character remains centered, and her hair-touching/turning action continues through the clip. The opening framing and subject placement closely match the provided reference image.
arguments.requested_change: Switch to a full-body 360-degree orbit camera that starts in front, circles the person, and returns to the front, using the reference for initial direction, placement, and framing while preserving the person's identity, appearance, action, timing, and scene.
uncertain: Whether the orbit completes exactly 360 degrees and returns precisely to the original front view is difficult to confirm from the sampled frames.
unexpected_changes: The scene changed from the source's mostly empty paved area to a detailed amusement-park environment with a Ferris wheel, stalls, and fences, although this matches the provided reference.
